description: Haarlemmerstraat cornice shop houses of four storeys: 4.2-7.6 m fronts of red-brown or painted brick, a shop ground storey to 3.8-4.4 m and three upper storeys of 2.4-2.7 m with white-framed windows, under a white cornice (often with dentils or a tall frieze) whose top stands at 12-13.2 m, sometimes one dormer over the middle; the upper windows are white small-pane sashes (6-over-6), usually three axes on a 4.6-4.8 m front

match.note: Haarlemmerstraat 46-54 (2024-11-21 strip, 1 m grid): the same storey grammar as the Haarlemmerdijk shop houses with small-pane sashes; two or three axes on one width, so reviewer bays pins (reviewBays.ts) count them. Haarlemmerdijk 21 and 33 (2024-12-11 strip, 1 m grid): shop fascia 3.7-4.4 m; rows 4.0-6.0 / 6.75-8.6 / 9.4-10.75 m (21) and 4.6-6.6 / 7.3-8.9 / 9.6-11.0 m (33); cornice tops 12.4 and 13.1 m. A separate type rather than a storey count from the eaves: the tall shop ground makes a three-storey front at 11.6 m and a four-storey one at 12.4 m indistinguishable by pitch; reviewer type pins pick it. Years 1600-1995: BAG dates restored fronts by their rebuild (Haarlemmerstraat 48B: 1984 behind an 18th-c. bell gable); every placement here is a reviewer type pin. eavesM [11.0, 13.0] sets the storey pitch from the measured fronts (46: cornice 12.0 m over four storeys (3.0 m pitch)); one storey count per type, picked by reviewer type pins

dormer.note: Haarlemmerdijk 6 (176172), 18 (167817): one white dormer over the middle

door-left.note: residential ground: house door on the left axis; shops come per pand from BAG/OSM (autoShopfront)

roof.evidence: Haarlemmerdijk 6, 33, 35A (2022-12-15 strips): sky stands directly over the cornice and the dormer, no roof face over the cornice; the 3DBAG front attic at 30 deg drew a red band the strips never show. Canal-house saddles run front to back (hip front); pitch 35 deg keeps the hipped face over the cornice to about 1.4 m on a 4-5 m front (50 deg drew a 2.7 m red triangle the strips never show)

rhythm.windowsPerStorey: ground: a shop (BAG/OSM) or a house door and window | upper: 2 or 3
rhythm.groundFloor: a tall shop ground 4.4-4.9 m to the fascia top on the dijk and straat
rhythm.roofline: a plain white cornice, sometimes one dormer
schemaLimits: the cornice frieze and consoles are a plain slab
